about: A request of the Mesh https binding signed under the `key` authenticator (SCE_MESH.md section
22.9; docs/adr/0109, D9), which the C++ client and the Rust host core agree on byte for byte.
The values were computed apart from both, with libsodium's Ed25519 through PyNaCl.
`seed` is the Ed25519 seed the client's host generated, `public_key` its public key; every
hexadecimal value is the bytes it spells. The client posts `body` to `url`, whose target URI as a
signature covers it is `target_uri`, with the fields `headers`, at `created` (seconds since the
Unix epoch). Signing it must add exactly the fields `signed`, in that order: the key it offers
(the COSE_Key of RFC 9679's thumbprint input, base64url), the Signature-Input whose keyid is that
The C++ client's RequestSigner signs these inputs into `signed`; the Rust server's verification
takes the request whole (`headers` and `signed`) under the offered key at `created`, and refuses
it with a covered field changed.
